sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Sajeet Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.587 of 2023, under Section 498A, 304B, 302 IPC & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Nanpara, District Bahraich.

3. It is argued by learned counsel for the applicant that arising out of the same incident, the mother-in-law and father-in-law of the deceased have been enlarged on bail vide orders dated Monu Soni vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ...

entities.text: Monu Soni vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was married to the applicant two years ago and subsequently, on 24.09.2023, the entire matrimonial family had killed the daughter.
The cause of death, as per the postmortem report, is ante mortem strangulation.
It is argued by counsel for the applicant that the applicant is in custody since 28.09.2023 having no criminal history and there is nothing specific against the applicant.
However, considering the fact that the trial has not even started and the applicant has already suffered pre-trial detention of more than six months, he may be enlarged on bail.

5. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application by arguing that the death had occurred within three years of marriage and considering the postmortem report which indicates the cause of death as ante mortem strangulation and the fact that the applicant is the husband, no case for bail is made out.
However, he does not dispute that the applicant has no criminal history.

6. Considering the submissions made at the Bar, in terms of the postmortem report, the cause of death is ante mortem strangulation and a specific allegation against the applicant is not prima-facie evident, as such, considering the fact that the trial has not even started and the applicant has suffered pre-trial detention of six months coupled with the fact that there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant, if enlarged on bail, can in any way adversely affect the trial, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Monu Soni be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 15.4.2024 nishant  Monu Soni vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ... on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151797339/
